How a detection works

Method, as implemented in anomaly_mitigation.py

Detection is statistical, not a fixed threshold on a magic number. Each traffic source is compared with its own rolling history: a surge is a rate far above that source's rolling mean in standard-deviation terms, and an elephant flow is a single source whose share of the concurrent traffic crosses the share the caller configured while also sitting above its own baseline. An elephant needs at least two observed sources — a lone source is always 100% of itself and proves nothing.

Every verdict is logged as an anomaly_detected control event whose reason string carries the kind, the link, and the measurements behind the verdict. This page parses those recorded strings back apart — it does not re-run the detector on old data — so what is shown here is exactly what the controller saw at the time.

A detection is a record, not automatically an action: the mitigation decision (rate-limit the source back to its baseline) is produced as data, and the controller only installs it when anomaly mitigation is enabled for the run. Detections logged with mitigation off are still detections — they are the evidence the workload really contained abnormal traffic.
